title: The live Bourbon Street record in Toronto
summary: Toronto trio recorded by Don Thompson.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Another album in that general timeframe was almost the opposite in how it came to be. I think that Don Thompson may have just put a tape recorder across the
We played at this club in Toronto. Oh, it was funny. I had gone up there a few times to work. Tell me the name of the club ‘cause it’s on…

Bourbon Street, yeah. And I would always take a bass player from New York or something with me. And then, I went to… Ed Bickert was a dear friend and marvelous guitar player, who ended up playing with Desmond and everything. I went over to Ed’s house once for a jam session and Don Thompson and Terry Clarke were there, and I said, “Why am I take… bringing musicians from New York?” So… we… I’ve worked with Don and Terry. That’s how we hooked up. And Don just put recording equipment on the stage, and we were there for a couple of weeks, and he recorded the whole thing, and that’s how that record happened. But again, people insist that it must… you know, must have had this great engineer come, and Don just set up a couple mics. (laughs) And yeah, he had the recording equipment there for the whole time. It was… So you hear… There’s one tune where… or a couple tunes where we play a silly ending or something
and we all crack up, and that’s because we… I didn’t even realize we were recording or I had forgotten. But it came out really nice, I think.
